chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abū Dāwūd, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from his brother al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:
I asked him whether the leftover water from any of the riding beasts may be drunk and used for wudu (ablution). He said: “As for camels and cattle, there is no problem.”

key_terms.الدَّوَابِّ: beasts or animals, especially riding or domestic animals
key_terms.سُؤْرُ: leftover water or drink remaining after an animal has drunk from it
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can the leftover water of camels and cattle be drunk or used for wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a fiqh ruling concerning the leftover water drunk from by animals and whether it may still be used for drinking and wudu (ablution). It states that the leftover water of camels and cattle is unobjectionable, indicating its permissibility for such use.
